summary: Regional routing commit gap causes intermittent model-pin revert during zero-downtime rollout
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged zero-downtime canary rollout for Tellus Analytics (dedicated customer), a subset of tenant sessions briefly reverted to the previously pinned model for up to 14s despite an apparent successful control-plane commit. Impact: customers observed mixed responses (quality deviation) and increased token costs while sessions retried.

Impact:
- Intermittent mixed-model responses for ~3% of requests from the affected tenant over a 12-minute window.
- Increased support tickets and regression alerts on Tellus eval set.
- Reproduces only during rollouts that overlap a regional routing table apply + edge-cache flush window.

Environment:
- Prod (us-west primary, us-east failover).
- Tenant on Dedicated pool with pinned model gpt-redwood-1.2 promoted to redwood-opus-7b-8bit (canary 10% -> 100%).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Start canary promote of new model variant via Console (10% weight to 100% over 10m).
2. Control plane commits candidate snapshot for routing; orchestrator applies to regional route shards sequentially (us-west then us-east).
3. Edge proxy shard A receives new snapshot and invalidates local pin cache. Edge proxy shard B still serving old snapshot for a short TTL window.
4. Concurrent session-affinity tokens originating during the handover hit mixed shards and are redirected to the old variant before their pin was persisted.
5. Fallback logic kicks in for a few requests causing visible revert to previous model for those sessions.

Observed behavior:
- Pin commit confirmed in control-plane logs but not acknowledged by all regional route shards before edge cache TTL expired.
- Edge-level requests show 14s windows where routing returned legacy variant.
- No 5xx errors; behavior is routing-level inconsistency.

Expected behavior:
- Either atomic pin commit across all active shards or transparent transient fallback that keeps sessions on the intended variant until consistency reached.

Logs / artifacts:
- Control-plane commit: controller-logs://commit/2026-03-10T16:02:11Z (commit-id: c2f3b9)
- Edge-proxy shard logs: edge-us-west-01 and edge-us-west-02 (attached in internal bundle)
- Trace sample: tracing.redwood/prod/trace/7b3a9df2 (shows route decision flip)
- Customer evidence: Tellus provided three request IDs with mixed outputs.

Immediate mitigation taken:
- Support escalated to SRE and toggled conservative rollout (paused weight increase) at 16:07 UTC.
- Performed targeted edge cache flush for tenant on us-west to remove stale snapshot (manual flush via admin API).
- Alerted Tellus and asked to hold further high-volume workloads until stabilized.

Current status:
- Canary paused; no further mixed-responses detected after edge flush and controlled pause.
- Engineering is investigating control-plane->edge ack path and shard apply ordering.
comments: 2026-03-10 16:10 UTC - Support (Maya): Initial triage complete. Paused rollout and flushed edge cache for tenant. Asking SRE to look for inter-shard commit gaps.

2026-03-10 16:22 UTC - SRE (Diego): Found control-plane applied snapshot to us-west then us-east; us-east apply lagged by ~11s. Edge shard TTLs 15s allowed transient routing to use old snapshot. Collecting logs from routecoordinator and edge cache metrics.

2026-03-10 17:05 UTC - Eng (Lina Patel): Reproduced locally with staging cluster using manual shard-apply ordering; confirmed race between shard apply ack and edge cache TTL leads to short revert window when session-affinity tokens are proxied across shards.

2026-03-10 18:12 UTC - Support (Maya): Notified customer (Tellus Analytics) about pause and mitigation steps. Customer reported no new regressions after actions. They requested a permanent fix and a postmortem.

2026-03-11 09:40 UTC - Eng (Lina): Draft hotfix branch created for routecoordinator: add per-commit barrier that waits for all shard-apply acks before exposing commit to edge (PR referenced). Further discussion about backwards-compatible rollout needed.
2026-03-12 11:15 UTC - Product (Ethan): Prioritizing hotfix as P1 for Dedicated customers with strict pinning SLAs. Scheduling code review and small-canary deploy of coordinator change.

2026-03-12 14:02 UTC - SRE (Diego): Running extended verification in staging across multi-region shards with synthetic session tokens. No regressions so far. Planning controlled deploy to canary pool tonight.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: The orchestrator committed new routing snapshots but returned success to the control-plane before all regional shards had acknowledged apply; edge proxies used previously cached snapshot for up to their TTL causing transient routing using legacy variant. Evidence: apply timestamps show ~11s delta; edge cache TTLs default to 15s. Reproducible in staging by intentionally delaying shard apply. Potential contributing factor: session-affinity tokens proxied across shards without robust revalidation when snapshot changes mid-session.
resolution: Mitigation applied: paused rollout and flushed edge caches for affected tenant, preventing further mixed outputs. Next steps: implement coordinator barrier (PR 2042) that requires ack from all active shards before marking commit visible to edge; reduce default edge cache TTL for pin metadata to 5s; add an observability metric for 'pin-commit-ack-lag' and an SLO. Plan: ship hotfix to canary pool 2026-03-13 and full rollout 2026-03-15 if green. Customer follow-up: schedule postmortem and share remediation timeline.
next_steps: Merge PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/routecoordinator/pull/2042 and deploy to canary pool
Lower edge pin-metadata TTL to 5s behind feature flag
Coordinate postmortem with Tellus and publish RCA to Confluence
